newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan investors sell Canadian dlrs for yen - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Japan investors sell Canadian dlrs for yen - dealers.

text.p: Japanese investors, including a major public fund body, have apparently been selling Canadian dollars for yen ahead of the redemption of Canadian government bonds in March, currency dealers said on Wednesday.

A Canadian banking source in Tokyo said a public fund had been actively selling Canadian dollars for yen recently, probably to prepare for the maturity of 10-year Canadian government bonds on March 1.
The maturing bonds carry a coupon of 8.25 percent, and the outstanding issue amount is C$3.4 billion.
Japanese investors were eager to invest in high-yielding bonds during a foreign bond investment boom in the late 1980s.

Investors, particularly public investment bodies, have a tendency to hold bonds until maturity and some of them are thought to be holding a substantial amount of maturing Canadian bonds, dealers said.

"Sales of Canadian dollars for yen have been detected since the start of this week and the moves are aimed at switching a portion of the maturing funds into U.S. Treasuries," said the Canadian bank source.
The source said the yield curve of the Canadian government bond market was currently steeper than that of the U.S. Treasury bond.
This means that investors wary of holding long-term securities may prefer to invest in U.S. Treasuries which may give investors higher returns and carry less of a risk.

A major Japanese public fund, possibly the Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo), has continued to buy huge amounts of short-term U.S. government securities and U.S. dollars since the end of January, currency dealers said.
They said that the public fund buying was a driving force behind the dollar"s rise against the yen.
Kampo might be among the investors switching their Canadian bond investments to U.S. Treasuries, although one bond dealer cited other institutions as well.
Kampo customarily does not comment on details of its investments.
